jobs.title: Upgrade: Développeur(-euse) Expérience IA (IA conversationnelle)
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Canada (Remote)

Upgrade aide ses clients à avancer dans la bonne direction grâce à des produits financiers abordables et responsables. Depuis 2017, nous avons aidé plus de 7,5 millions de clients à accéder à plus de 42 milliards de dollars en crédit à la consommation. En nous concentrant sans relâche sur l'amélioration du bien-être financier de nos clients, nous développons des produits qui leur permettent de faire des économies et qui les soutiennent pour un meilleur avenir financier. Nous sommes soutenus par certains des meilleurs investisseurs dans le domaine de la technologie et avons été récemment valorisés à 7,3 milliards de dollars.

Nous sommes constamment reconnus pour notre culture de collaboration et d'inclusion. Plus récemment, nous avons été classés parmi les Premières entreprises fintech au monde par CNBC, Meilleurs lieux de travail par Built In, et par le San Francisco Business Times, Meilleurs lieux de travail d'Amérique par Newsweek, Meilleur employeur ''Startup'' par Forbes, et Employeurs les plus sains par Phoenix Business Journal.

Nous recherchons de nouveaux membres d'équipe qui sont enthousiastes à l'idée de concevoir et de proposer des produits nouveaux et meilleurs. Rejoignez-nous et aidez à bâtir un meilleur avenir financier pour des millions de personnes.

À propos du rôle

Un(e) Développeur(-euse) Expérience IA est responsable du cycle de vie complet des parcours que nos clients vivent avec l'agent IA d'Upgrade par clavardage, par téléphone et par courriel : création, optimisation, gestion des cas particuliers et augmentation du taux de résolution autonome. Cette personne conçoit des parcours dans les outils sans code de Sierra, collabore avec les groupes produits d'Upgrade pour intégrer leurs processus de service à l'agent, et répond de la capacité de l'agent à résoudre le problème du client de façon sécuritaire, exacte et sans intervention humaine.

Nous recherchons un(e) Développeur(-euse) Expérience IA pour prendre en charge l'agent IA d'Upgrade destiné à la clientèle. Vous ferez le lien entre les équipes de développement, de produit et des opérations clientèle. Vous transformerez des processus de service, comme effectuer un paiement, consulter les détails d'un prêt, mettre à jour une adresse ou activer les paiements préautorisés, en parcours de production, et vous continuerez à les améliorer après leur lancement.

Vous concevrez et gérerez les parcours de A à Z, de la première ébauche jusqu'à leur pleine maturité. Le travail est à la fois celui d'un bâtisseur et d'un analyste : concevoir le parcours, gérer les cas particuliers, lire les transcriptions et augmenter continuellement le taux de résolution autonome. Le taux de résolution autonome, la satisfaction client (CSAT), la qualité des transferts et le taux d'hallucination sont vos indicateurs clés. Au cours de votre première année, vous serez responsable d'un portefeuille de parcours couvrant l'ensemble de nos produits (prêts personnels, carte, paiement différé (BNPL), marge de crédit hypothécaire (HELOC), dépôts) et contribuerez à établir les normes selon lesquelles Upgrade conçoit, teste et déploie ses expériences IA.

Nos technologies principales

Sierra Agent Studio (parcours sans code), simulations et analyse des conversations Sierra, API GraphQL et REST (comme outils de parcours), Genesys (transfert vers le centre de contact), SumoLogic, Grafana, SQL, JavaScript/TypeScript, Claude et autres outils de LLM.

Ce que vous ferez

  • Création de parcours : Concevoir et développer des parcours Sierra dans Agent Studio pour le clavardage, la voix et le courriel, de la phase de découverte avec les opérations jusqu'au déploiement en production
  • Optimisation : Analyser chaque semaine les transcriptions, les enregistrements et les données analytiques, repérer où les conversations échouent ou sont transférées, et déployer des correctifs à la logique des parcours, aux instructions et à la base de connaissances
  • Gestion des cas particuliers : Cartographier les scénarios problématiques (paiements refusés, identité non concordante, comptes en souffrance, demandes non prises en charge) et s'assurer que chacun se conclut par une réponse exacte ou un transfert fluide
  • Résolution autonome : Assumer la responsabilité des cibles de résolution autonome et de CSAT pour chaque parcours, mener des déploiements progressifs (1 % → 100 %) et prioriser les travaux ayant le plus d'impact sur ces indicateurs
  • Partenariat produit : Collaborer avec les groupes produits (prêts personnels, carte, BNPL, dépôts) pour définir la portée de nouveaux parcours, maintenir les parcours à jour au fil de l'évolution des produits et définir les API dont l'agent a besoin
  • Sécurité et conformité : Appliquer l'authentification à plusieurs niveaux et la vérification renforcée, le libellé de conformité exact ainsi que des garde-fous contre les hallucinations et les réponses non conformes aux politiques
  • Transferts : Concevoir les transferts vers des agents humains dans Genesys avec des résumés exacts et le contexte d'authentification
  • Tests : Créer des suites de simulation et de tests de régression afin que chaque modification de parcours soit déployée avec la preuve qu'elle n'altère pas le comportement existant
  • Surveillance : Suivre la latence, les erreurs et les abandons dans SumoLogic et Grafana, et être responsable des alertes
  • Optimisation vocale : Latence, phrases de transition, interruptions, personnalité et ton
  • Relation avec Sierra : Agir à titre de responsable technique de notre côté, faire remonter les problèmes liés à la plateforme et orienter les demandes relatives à la feuille de route

Ce que nous recherchons

  • De 3 à 5 ans d'expérience en développement logiciel, ou une expérience équivalente dans des rôles en solutions techniques, en IA conversationnelle ou en gestion de produits techniques
  • Connaissance pratique du comportement des agents LLM : instructions, appels d'outils, récupération de connaissances, et les points de défaillance de chacun
  • Expérience dans la conception d'évaluations pour des systèmes non déterministes : jeux de tests, simulations, LLM évaluateur (LLM-as-judge), seuils de régression
  • Une maîtrise technique suffisante pour lire des spécifications d'API, collaborer avec des développeurs backend sur des intégrations REST et GraphQL, et raisonner sur les autorisations et les portées de permissions
  • Un esprit axé sur le produit et le client : vous comprenez les procédures opérationnelles, lisez les transcriptions, accordez de l'importance au ton et mesurez votre réussite selon la résolution du problème du client
  • Sens des responsabilités en production : déploiements, surveillance, analyse de journaux et réponse aux incidents
  • Rédaction claire et capacité à travailler avec des interlocuteurs non techniques des équipes des opérations, de la conformité et des affaires juridiques

Atouts supplémentaires

  • Expérience pratique de Sierra Agent Studio ou d'une plateforme d'agents sans code comparable (Decagon, Ada, Kore.ai, Google CCAI, Amazon Lex/Connect)
  • Expérience en IA vocale : reconnaissance vocale (speech-to-text), synthèse vocale (text-to-speech), optimisation de la latence, gestion des interruptions (barge-in)
  • Connaissance des systèmes de centre de contact tels que Genesys et de la conception de transferts vers des agents
  • Expérience en fintech ou dans un autre secteur réglementé (UDAAP, FDCPA, TCPA, PCI, SOC 2)
  • Expérience en conception conversationnelle ou en rédaction UX

Ce que nous vous offrons

  • Salaire compétitif ($140K-$180K) et plan d'options d'achat d'actions
  • Assurances médicales, dentaires et de la vue payées par l'entreprise
  • Congés payés flexibles
  • Possibilités de croissance et de développement professionnel
  • Congé parental payé
  • Initiatives de santé et de bien-être

Exigence linguistique

English language is required for this position, as it involves interacting with staff at Upgrade's offices worldwide.

L'anglais est requis pour ce poste, puisqu'il comporte des interactions avec le personnel des bureaux d'Upgrade à l'échelle internationale.

Conditions environnementales et de travail

Le travail s'effectue à l'intérieur dans un environnement au rythme soutenu qui exige la capacité de gérer plusieurs priorités et de respecter les processus de travail, les horaires et les attentes en matière de service établi.

Les employés saisissent, extraient et échangent régulièrement des informations avec précision à l'aide de systèmes et d'applications numériques afin d'appuyer les objectifs opérationnels et de service à la clientèle.

Le poste exige la capacité de recevoir et d'échanger des informations avec les clients, les collègues, les superviseurs et les partenaires interfonctionnels par le biais des moyens de communication disponibles, qui peuvent inclure des réunions, des courriels, des appels téléphoniques et des outils de collaboration numériques, et peut impliquer des échanges en temps réel, verbaux ou en personne selon les besoins de l'entreprise.

Les fonctions peuvent inclure la gestion d'un volume élevé d'interactions entrantes et/ou sortantes avec la clientèle ainsi que d'activités de travail à l'aide de systèmes de télécommunication et informatiques. Le poste exige la capacité de lire, d'analyser et d'interpréter les informations affichées à l'écran d'ordinateur et de maintenir une posture de travail pendant de longues périodes, conformément aux exigences du poste.

Le travail peut s'effectuer dans un centre de contact, un bureau ou en télétravail, selon les besoins de l'entreprise et la nature du poste. Les environnements de travail sur place peuvent inclure des espaces de travail partagés, un éclairage de bureau standard et un bruit de fond modéré typique des environnements de service à la clientèle ou opérationnels.

Les employés en télétravail sont responsables de maintenir un espace de travail sécurisé et productif avec une connexion Internet fiable qui prend en charge les systèmes de l'entreprise et protège la confidentialité des informations de l'entreprise et des clients.

Des mesures d'adaptation raisonnables peuvent être mises en place pour permettre aux personnes qualifiées vivant avec un handicap d'exercer les fonctions essentielles du poste, conformément à l'Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) et aux lois étatiques et locales applicables.

Nous sommes un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances et nous valorisons la diversité au sein de notre entreprise. Nous ne faisons pas de discrimination fondée sur la race, la religion, la couleur, l'origine nationale, le sexe, l'orientation sexuelle, l'âge, l'état civil, le statut d'ancien combattant ou le statut de handicap.

Upgrade n'accepte pas les candidatures spontanées soumises par des agences de recrutement, des cabinets de recherche de personnel ou toute autre tierce partie. Tout CV soumis à un employé d'Upgrade sans accord écrit préalable en vigueur sera considéré comme la propriété d'Upgrade, et Upgrade ne sera pas tenue de payer des bonus de recommandation ou de placement. Les agences doivent obtenir une approbation écrite au préalable du service d'acquisition de talents d'Upgrade pour soumettre des candidatures, et ce, seulement si une entente valide et dûment signée est en vigueur.

jobs.title: Lattice: Senior Contracts Manager
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote - US

This is Legal at Lattice

The Lattice Legal team is looking for an experienced, business-minded Senior Contracts Manager to help lead our commercial contracting function. In this role, you will independently manage a broad portfolio of customer, vendor, partnership, and other commercial agreements while serving as a trusted adviser to teams across the company.

You will be expected to understand Lattice’s business, products, contracting standards, and risk framework well enough to resolve most matters independently, identify practical paths through difficult negotiations, and escalate issues with a clear assessment and recommendation. The right candidate combines strong contract judgment, operational discipline, commercial awareness, and fluency with modern legal technology and AI-assisted workflows.

This is a highly cross-functional role supporting Sales, Deal Desk, Procurement, Privacy, Security, Finance, Product, Partnerships, Marketing, and other business teams. Success requires balancing thoughtful risk management with a practical focus on customer experience, business velocity, and scalable operations.

What You Will Do

  • Independently draft, review, negotiate, and manage a high volume of commercial agreements within Lattice’s contracting playbooks, approval framework, and risk tolerances.
  • Lead negotiations involving SaaS order forms, terms of service, master services agreements, data processing agreements, service level agreements, amendments, renewals, trials, AI-related terms, termination agreements, and related customer documents.
  • Review and negotiate vendor, supplier, and service-provider agreements, coordinating with Procurement, Privacy, Security, Finance, and business owners based on the services involved and the risks presented.
  • Support technology partnerships, integrations, referral programs, sponsorships, events, speaker engagements, and other strategic or marketing relationships.
  • Serve as a primary point of contact between Legal and business stakeholders, providing practical guidance on contract structure, risk allocation, negotiation strategy, approval requirements, and escalation paths.
  • Exercise independent judgment to resolve matters within established parameters and promptly escalate material legal, financial, privacy, security, product, or operational risks with a concise analysis and recommended approach.
  • Partner with Privacy, Security, Product, Finance, and other subject-matter experts to ensure contractual commitments are accurate, operationally feasible, properly approved, and tracked where appropriate.
  • Manage numerous concurrent negotiations with strong prioritization, responsiveness, and ownership from intake through signature.
  • Maintain accurate contract records, approvals, metadata, and final documentation across Ironclad, Salesforce, Zip, and related systems.
  • Identify recurring negotiation patterns, operational friction, and emerging risks, and translate those observations into improvements to templates, playbooks, fallback positions, training, and self-service resources.
  • Use approved AI and legal technology tools to accelerate contract review, compare proposed language against playbooks, identify issues, support drafting, summarize negotiations, and improve reporting and workflow efficiency.
  • Help develop meaningful reporting on contract volume, cycle time, negotiation trends, escalations, and other indicators that can improve the contracting function and the broader business.
  • Stay informed about developments affecting commercial contracting, SaaS businesses, data privacy, AI-enabled products, and contracting technology.

What You Will Bring to the Table

  • Five or more years of relevant experience negotiating and managing commercial technology agreements, preferably in a high-growth SaaS or technology company. Equivalent combinations of legal, contracts, and business experience will be considered.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage customer-facing SaaS negotiations, including master agreements, subscription terms, data processing agreements, service level agreements, and related commercial documents.
  • Experience reviewing technology vendor and procurement agreements. 
  • Strong commercial judgment and the ability to distinguish material risk from lower-value negotiating points.
  • Ability to apply playbooks and policies thoughtfully, identify matters outside established parameters, and present escalation issues with practical recommendations.
  • Working knowledge of common SaaS contracting issues, including intellectual property, confidentiality, data use, privacy, security, indemnification, limitations of liability, SLAs, warranties, renewals, and termination rights.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex contract issues clearly to business stakeholders and counterparties.
  • Excellent organizational and project-management skills, with demonstrated success managing a large and changing portfolio of matters with limited supervision.
  • A collaborative approach and a record of building trusted relationships across Sales, Deal Desk, Procurement, Finance, Privacy, Security, Product, and other functions.
  • Meaningful experience using AI-assisted tools for contract review, drafting, analysis, knowledge management, or workflow automation, together with sound judgment regarding confidentiality, accuracy, and responsible use.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Word and experience with contract lifecycle management and procurement platforms.
  • Experience with Ironclad, Salesforce, Zip, Google Workspace, Slack, and Excel is preferred.
  • Experience working with international counterparties and modern privacy and AI regulatory frameworks is a plus.

__

The estimated annual cash salary for this role is $123,500 - $154,500. This position is also eligible for incentive stock options, subject to the terms of Lattice’s applicable plans.

Benefits: The Company offers the following benefits for this position, subject to applicable eligibility requirements: Medical insurance; Dental insurance; Vision insurance; Life, AD&D, and Disability Insurance; Emergency Weather Support; Wellness Apps; Paid Parental Leave, Paid Time off inclusive of holidays and sick time; Commuter & Parking Accounts; Lunches in the Office; Workplace Amenities Stipend, Internet and Phone Stipend; 401(k) retirement plan; Financial Planning; Learning & Development Budget

*Note on Pay Transparency:

Lattice provides an estimate of the compensation for roles that may be hired as required by state regulations. Compensation may vary based on (a) location, as Lattice factors in specific location when benchmarking compensation for most roles; (b) individual candidate skills and qualifications; and (c) individual candidate experience.

Additionally, Lattice leverages current market data to determine compensation, so posted compensation figures are subject to change as new market data becomes available. The salary, other compensation, and benefits information is accurate as of the date of this posting. Lattice reserves the right to modify this information at any time, subject to applicable law.

#LI-remote

About Lattice

jobs.title: Upgrade: AI Experience Engineer (Conversational AI)
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Canada (Remote)

About the Role:

An AI Experience Engineer owns the full lifecycle of the journeys our customers have with Upgrade's AI agent on chat, voice and email: creation, optimization, edge case handling and containment growth. They build journeys in Sierra's no-code tooling, partner with Upgrade's product groups to bring their servicing flows to the agent, and are accountable for whether the agent resolves the customer's issue safely, accurately and without a human.

We are hiring an AI Experience Engineer to own Upgrade's customer-facing AI agent. You will sit between engineering, product and customer operations. You will turn servicing workflows, such as making a payment, checking loan details, updating an address or enabling autopay, into production journeys and keep improving them after launch. You will build and own the journeys end to end, from first draft to steady state. The work is part builder, part analyst: design the flow, handle the edge cases, read the transcripts, and keep raising containment. Containment, CSAT, transfer quality and hallucination rate are your metrics.

Within your first year, you will own a portfolio of journeys across products (Personal Loans, Card, BNPL, HELOC, Deposits) and help set the standards for how Upgrade builds, tests and ships AI experiences.

 

Our Core Technologies

Sierra Agent Studio (no-code journeys), Sierra simulations and conversation analytics, GraphQL and REST APIs (as journey tools), Genesys (contact center handoff), SumoLogic, Grafana, SQL, Javascript/Typescript, Claude and other LLM tools.

 

What You'll Do

• Journey creation: Design and build Sierra journeys in Agent Studio for chat, voice and email, from discovery with operations through production rollout

• Optimization: Review transcripts, recordings and analytics every week, find where conversations fail or transfer, and ship fixes to journey logic, instructions and knowledge

• Edge case handling: Map the unhappy paths (failed payments, mismatched identity, delinquent accounts, unsupported requests) and make sure each ends in a correct answer or a clean handoff

• Containment: Own containment and CSAT targets per journey, run staged rollouts (1% → 100%), and prioritize the work that moves those numbers most

• Product partnership: Work with product groups (Personal Loans, Card, BNPL, Deposits) to scope new journeys, keep journeys current as products change, and define the APIs the agent needs

• Safety and compliance: Apply tiered authentication and step-up verification, verbatim compliance language and guardrails against hallucination and off-policy answers

• Handoffs: Design transfers to human agents in Genesys with accurate summaries and auth context

• Testing: Build simulation and regression suites so every journey change ships with evidence it did not break existing behavior

• Monitoring: Watch latency, errors and drop-offs in SumoLogic and Grafana, and own the alerts

• Voice tuning: Latency, filler phrases, interruptions, personality and tone

• Sierra relationship: Be the technical owner on our side, escalate platform issues and shape roadmap asks

 

What We Look For:

• 3–5 years of Frontend Software Engineering experience, or equivalent experience in Solutions Engineering, Conversational AI or Technical Product roles

• Working knowledge of how LLM agents behave: instructions, tool calls, knowledge retrieval, and where each one fails

• Experience building evaluations for non-deterministic systems: test sets, simulations, LLM-as-judge, regression gates

• Enough technical depth to read API specs, work with backend engineers on REST and GraphQL integrations, and reason about authorization and permission scopes

• Working knowledge of JavaScript/TypeScript, with the ability to build and maintain coded journeys and integrate APIs within conversational AI platforms.

• Product and customer mindset: you understand ops procedures, you read transcripts, care about tone, and measure success by whether the customer's problem got solved

• Ownership in production: rollouts, monitoring, log analysis and incident response

• Clear writing and the ability to work with non-engineers in operations, compliance and legal

 

Nice To Have:

• Hands-on experience with Sierra Agent Studio, or a comparable no-code agent platform (Decagon, Ada, Kore.ai, Google CCAI, Amazon Lex/Connect)

• Voice AI experience: speech-to-text, text-to-speech, latency tuning, barge-in handling

• Contact center systems such as Genesys, and agent handoff design

• Background in fintech or another regulated industry (UDAAP, FDCPA, TCPA, PCI, SOC 2)

• Conversation design or UX writing experience

 

What We Offer You: 

• Competitive salary ($140K-$180K CAN) and stock option plan

• Paid coverage of medical, dental and vision insurance 

• Flexible PTO

• Opportunities for professional growth and development
• Paid parental leave

• Health & wellness initiatives

jobs.title: Customer.io: Email Deliverability Specialist
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Americas Remote

About Customer.io

Over 9,000 companies — from scrappy startups to global brands — use our platform to send billions of emails, push notifications, in-app messages, and SMS every day. Customer.io powers automated communication that people actually want to receive. We help teams send smarter, more relevant messages using real-time behavioral data.

About the role

Hi, my name is Caitlin, Senior Manager, Technical Support at Customer.io, and I'm looking for an Email Deliverability Specialist to join our deliverability program within Technical Support. You'll help customers reach the inbox by diagnosing sending issues, advising on best practices, and guiding senders through an email ecosystem that keeps changing.

You'll be one of several deliverability experts on a team that shares knowledge across Technical Support, so your work reaches well beyond your own queue. You'll partner with Customer Success, Technical Support, and Engineering: taking customer calls, equipping CSMs for customer conversations, working through complex technical cases alongside Engineering, and turning what you see in tickets into documentation, training, and better processes.

You'll thrive here if you think about the health of the whole program, enjoy improving how work gets done, and are equally comfortable digging into a detailed case and having a direct conversation with a customer about acceptable use.

What we value

Empathy and curiosity: You approach every customer with patience and a desire to dig deeper, especially when a conversation gets uncomfortable.

Clarity: You explain complex technical concepts simply and help others do the same.

Collaboration: You build strong partnerships across Support, Customer Success, and Engineering, and you treat customer outcomes as a shared goal.

Thinking at scale: You look at how we do things today and see what could work better for the whole organization, then you help make it happen.

Continuous learning: You stay ahead of evolving standards and see change as a chance to improve how we work.

What you'll do

  • Act as a trusted deliverability advisor to customers, handling complex cases through to full resolution and leading customer calls when a conversation needs it
  • Audit sender setup and monitor reputation across IPs and domains, using authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and BIMI, DNS configuration, and provider tools like Google Postmaster Tools, Yahoo Sender Hub, and Microsoft SNDS to diagnose blocklists, spam traps, and engagement drops
  • Work through highly technical issues with Engineering, taking ownership of the investigation first and sharing trends from customer cases with Product and Engineering
  • Identify acceptable use policy violations and spam complaints, hold clear and direct conversations with customers about compliance, and keep up with evolving standards (Gmail and Yahoo sender requirements, CAN-SPAM, GDPR)

  • Deep understanding of email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI) and infrastructure (SMTP, MTAs, DNS), with the technical comfort to work through complex issues with Engineering
  • Proficiency with provider data feeds (Google Postmaster Tools, Yahoo Sender Hub, Microsoft SNDS) and third-party deliverability monitoring tools like Everest, MXToolbox, or similar, and the analytical skill to turn bounce, engagement, and blocklist data into clear recommendations
  • Working knowledge of email compliance and acceptable use standards, and comfort having direct conversations with customers who are sending outside of them

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including comfort leading customer calls and simplifying technical concepts for any audience

jobs.title: Tebra: Senior Benefits Administrator
jobs.description:
Headquarters: United States - Remote

Tebra only initiates contact with candidates via email from an official Tebra email address (@tebra.com, @patientpop.com, or @kareo.com) or through our applicant tracking system, Greenhouse. We will only ask you to provide sensitive personal information through our official application portal — not via social media or text message. We do not conduct interviews via instant messaging.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced and analytical Senior Benefits Administrator to oversee the day-to-day administration and strategic alignment of our health and welfare plans. Reporting directly to the HR Operations Director, this role plays a pivotal part in managing our self-insured medical plan, monitoring plan performance, managing Third-Party Administrator (TPA) relationships, and ensuring compliance across all health and welfare offerings (medical, dental, vision, life, disability, 401K and wellness).

The ideal candidate possesses deep expertise in ERISA, HIPAA, and ACA compliance, strong data analytics capabilities to evaluate claim trends, and exceptional employee communication skills to deliver a seamless experience.

Your Area of Focus

Self-Insured Plan Oversight & Financial Management

  • Claims Analysis & Tracking: Monitor ongoing medical and prescription drug claims performance; identify trends, high-cost claimants, and cost-driver patterns in partnership with plan actuaries and brokers.
  • Stop-Loss Administration: Coordinate stop-loss policy renewals, track claims reaching individual/aggregate stop-loss thresholds, and submit reimbursement filings to carriers.
  • TPA & Vendor Governance: Oversee relationships with Third-Party Administrators (TPAs), Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs), and Benefits broker and carriers. Ensure operational execution according to SLAs.
  • Funding & Reconciliations: Partner with Payroll and Accounting to manage weekly/monthly billing, claims funding requests, reserve requirements (IBNR tracking), and employee contribution and invoice reconciliations.

Health & Welfare Plan Administration

  • Open Enrollment: Lead the annual Open Enrollment process, including system updates, open enrollment communications, employee informational sessions, and post-enrollment audits.
  • Life Events & Ongoing Administration: Manage day-to-day enrollment changes, qualifying life events (QLEs), dependent eligibility verifications, and COBRA processing.
  • Disability & Leave Coordination: Support short-term/long-term disability programs and align benefit premiums during active FMLA/LOA periods.

Compliance & Governance

  • Regulatory Reporting: Ensure strict compliance with federal and state regulations, including ERISA, ACA (1094/1095 reporting), HIPAA, COBRA, and FMLA.
  • Plan Documentation: Maintain updated Summary Plan Descriptions (SPDs), Summaries of Benefits and Coverage (SBCs), Plan Documents, and Form 5500 filings.
  • Nondiscrimination Testing: Coordinate annual 105(h) and Section 125 nondiscrimination testing with third-party compliance specialists.
  • Annual Benefits Audits: Lead annual 401K audit and execute dependent eligibility and enrollment audits throughout the year.

Employee Experience & Communications

  • Escalated Claims Support: Act as the primary point of contact for complex, escalated employee claims issues, serving as an advocate while maintaining plan governance.
  • Benefits Communication: Draft clear, accessible employee communications explaining self-insured plan features, cost-saving tools (e.g., telehealth, centers of excellence), and wellness incentive initiatives.

Your Professional Qualifications

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Finance, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).
  • 5 years of direct experience dedicated to health & welfare plan administration.
  • Demonstrated experience managing self-insured / self-funded medical plans, including working with stop-loss insurance, TPAs, and PBMs.
  • Professional Certifications (Preferred): CEBS (Certified Employee Benefit Specialist), SHRM-CP/SHRM-SCP, or PHR/SPHR.

Technical & Analytical Skills

  • HRIS Proficiency: Experience administering benefits using Workday.
  • Data & Excel Mastery: Advanced skills in MS Excel (Pivot Tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, data modeling) to analyze large sets of claims and census data.
  • Regulatory Depth: Deep functional knowledge of ERISA, ACA, HIPAA, COBRA, and IRS Section 125 rules.

Mercury is building a complete finance stack for startups. We work hard to create the easiest and safest banking* experience possible to simplify entrepreneurs' and business owners’ financial lives.The challenge is to do so while ensuring we protect Mercury, customers and the broader financial ecosystem from bad actors and harmful, illegal or unauthorized activities.

Our AML Investigations team is crucial in this mission and is responsible for detecting suspicious activity, conducting thorough investigations, and shutting down bad actors. This team is growing and we’re looking to hire an additional AML Risk Investigator to help us with Bank Partner Requests for Information, Transaction Monitoring, Financial Crime Investigations, Case Management and drafting Unusual Activity Reports. As a member of our Investigations team, you’ll help handle our transaction monitoring queues while balancing an eagle eye for risk with excellent user experience. To begin with, you’ll work to help make sure we have smart, risk-based monitoring in place and help build out our case management technology and processes.

You’ll need to learn how a really wide range of businesses work and bring your knowledge to bear on our processes and product. Some of this work is repetitive and requires close attention to detail, so we need someone who loves working fraud and anti-money laundering transaction queues and managing a variety of complex investigations.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

As part of the journey, we would expect you to:

  • Provide input as we implement new transaction monitoring rules and tune existing ones
  • Review AML, and other financial crime alerts in our transaction monitoring queue and take action as needed
  • Contact our users for information on their account usage and transactions
  • Work with our partners and internal team members to review and assess information received from users
  • Investigate and respond to Requests for Information (RFIs) from our Partner Banks, delivering clear, well-supported AML reviews on customer’s account activity
  • Decision user accounts as needed, including locking or closing accounts
  • Develop an understanding of expected activity for each type of user we work with
  • Document investigative findings and escalate unusual or potentially suspicious activity to our Partners for SAR consideration
  • Develop an unfailing eye for potential fraud or money laundering
  • Investigate tools that would make your job easier 
  • Write clear documentation on current processes and help train future teammates

Some things that might make you successful in a role like this:

  • Have experience in identifying money laundering, detecting fraud, or other financial crimes related behavior in banking, fintech, or other financial services through vendor AND in-house developed transaction monitoring rules 
  • Be fluent in the language of bank transactions, including ACH, check, debit card, credit card, and wire transfers, both domestic and international
  • Understand the business banking landscape and have familiarity with international activity and ownership
  • Exercise empathy and understanding when communicating with users

jobs.title: Airbnb: Operations Engineer, BizTech

Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

BizTech fosters culture and connection at Airbnb by providing reliable corporate tools, innovative products, and technical support for all teams. We drive technical breakthroughs and strategies that redefine what it means to belong anywhere, delivering greater value for the business and our people. The Global Operations team at BizTech manages production services across Airbnb’s corporate environment, delivering reliable operations through Observability, Incident Management, Core Operations, and AI-enabled automation. We partner across BizTech to scale service quality, efficiency, and resilience.

The Difference You Will Make:

As an Operations Engineer, you'll apply AI at the forefront of BizTech's operational health: using LLM-powered triage and intelligent automation to resolve tickets, speed up incident response, and build self-healing observability that catches problems before they escalate. AI fluency is core to this role, not an add-on. You'll prototype agentic workflows, embed AI into runbooks and diagnostics, and continuously look for repetitive work automation can take over. Success looks like a shrinking backlog of recurring ticket categories through AI-assisted automation, faster MTTR powered by intelligent alerting and root-cause suggestions, and dashboards/reporting enhanced with AI-driven insights that give stakeholders clear, trustworthy visibility into service health and data quality.

A Typical Day: 

  • Manage the ticket queue prioritizing and resolving requests while identifying recurring categories to automate or deflect
  • Participate in a rotating on-call and incident response schedule, including weekends, troubleshooting and documenting issues in real time
  • Build and maintain monitoring dashboards (Tableau, Superset, Grafana) that track service health, availability, and data quality, flagging gaps as they emerge
  • Use AI-assisted tools (e.g., Claude, Copilot) to speed up triage, root-cause analysis, scripting, and documentation — while knowing when a problem needs hands-on judgment instead
  • Write and maintain code in general-purpose languages (Python, Go, JavaScript, TypeScript, Bash) to automate operational workflows
  • Partner with global stakeholder teams to drive issues to resolution


Your Expertise:

  • 3+ years of experience with observability and metrics tooling (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, ElasticSearch)
  • 3+ years working with data querying and pipelines (e.g., SQL, Airflow, Trino, SQS)

  • Hands-on experience with CI/CD and automation tooling (e.g., Jenkins, ArgoCD, GitHub Actions) across AWS, GCP, or Oracle Cloud
  • Comfort working in ticket/workflow-driven environments using Jira and Confluence

Your Location

Companies like Mercury, Flex, and Novo rely on Lithic's developer-friendly APIs, direct network connections, and flawless reconciliation to launch and scale card programs in weeks, not years.

Position: Senior Software Engineer, Processing

We are hiring a Senior Software Engineer for our Processing team to lead Lithic’s next phase of growth.

The Processing team builds and maintains the real-time interfaces between Lithic and external payment networks. Every card authorization, clearing message, and settlement file flows through systems this team owns. The team manages both online and batch transaction flows across Mastercard, Visa, and Amex, along with transaction enrichment, disputes processing, and network compliance. jobs.title: Alloy: Client Enablement Lead
jobs.description:
Headquarters: New York City, Remote

Alloy is where you belong!

Alloy is the AI-powered identity and fraud prevention platform that accelerates onboarding, stops fraud, and scales compliance across the customer lifecycle so financial organizations can grow without limits. More than 900 of the world's leading financial institutions and fintechs trust Alloy for smarter risk management that drives growth.

Through our values: Be Bold, Go Fast, Collaborate, and Celebrate Our Differences, we are creating a workplace where you can grow, thrive, and belong. See how we’ve been continuously recognized and named one of Inc. Magazine’s Best Workplaces, Forbes America’s Best Startup Employers, Best Fintech to Work for by American Banker, year after year.

Check out our investors and read more about us here.

About the team

Alloy’s platform is complex and managed with high-touch support from Alloy’s Technical Solutions team. Customers that would like to ‘self-serve’ often struggle to build a clear mental model of how Alloy works and why, falling back to Alloy’s support teams to complete even simple tasks. Today, enablement is spread across multiple repositories and handled one-to-one by delivery teams, with inconsistent results. Only a handful of sophisticated and adventurous clients currently achieve a moderate amount of self-sufficiency.

This leader owns customer enablement across Alloy. This is not a technical writing role. It is a role that builds and runs the program behind enablement: capturing knowledge continuously, packaging it for the right audience at the right moment, running hands-on customer training sessions, and measuring what works.

The Customer Enablement Lead will report to the VP of Product Design. From within the Product team they will help fill gaps and challenging areas of the product while creating a powerful feedback loop between customers and designers to decrease those gaps and challenges over time. The Enablement Lead will form strong cross-functional connections with the Support, Delivery, Technical Success, Product Marketing, and Product Operations teams to ensure customers have a seamless and supported experience as they go live and as we release new features.

Alloy operates in a hybrid-work environment. We look to foster collaboration and community by having our local employees onsite three days a week. This role is open to both local and remote candidates in the US.

What you'll own

The initial scope of work for this role will include:

Close Critical Gaps

Audit the current state. Evaluate and consolidate existing resources (API docs, help articles, the learning center, in-product help, and delivery-built guides). Work with cross-functional partners to create any missing documentation and “Customer 101” program material.

Outcome: Our AI support bot can answer essentially any customer question. Our delivery teams can pull together the content they need to run tailored training sessions with their customers.

Deliver the Alloy New Customer Enablement Program

Focus on new Alloy customers and deliver scalable, deployable training and content for repeatable implementations. Structure material so clients can self-pace from foundational to advanced. Target key user personas so they learn the features critical to their respective day-to-day.

Outcome: Clients understand and use what they bought, and are aware of what else Alloy offers. Additionally they know where to look for additional guidance via documentation, AI support chat, and other escalation channels.

Build the Product Release Enablement Program

When Alloy builds a material new feature or capability, map what each client segment and persona needs to know, when, and why, from pre-sales through go-live and ongoing use, and make it part of how products are sold, launched, and delivered.

Outcome: a shared view of our friction points and what areas currently drag the most on our bottom line.

Facilitate the Feedback Loop

Collect feedback after every release, rollout, and training. Give Product, Design, and Delivery a shared view of where clients get stuck, and drive alignment on whether each gap is best solved by product, technical solutions, or enablement, including interim fixes.

Outcome: Product, Design, and Delivery share one view of enablement gaps and who owns them. The design team gets critical insight continuously, addressing customer confusion directly in the product, helping reduce the surface area for documentation over time.

Milestones

30 Days

Onboarding into Alloy, learning the product yourself, existing resource audit, gap analysis, start filling documentation gaps with SME and tooling support, and deliver a consolidation plan.

60 Days

Initial enablement ‘package’ in beta for first client feedback via early hands-on training sessions.

90 days

Initial enablement funnel for core segments deployed and documentation gap filling has demonstrated a measurable increase in AI support ticket resolution. Iteration on the enablement package incorporating early feedback.

Six Months

Enablement package is ‘production ready’ and universally rolled out (client-facing teams are ready to deliver training using the material). Feedback loop with product and design solidified. The product release enablement funnel is operational as part of new feature releases. Seeing measurable improvements in some areas of self-service and legacy support ticket theme avoidance.

Who we’re looking for

Must-haves:

  • 7+ years in customer education, enablement, or training, including building a customer enablement program from the ground up.
  • Experience enabling customers on a technical, API-driven B2B SaaS product, with the depth to learn complex workflows and teach them clearly.
  • Strong live facilitation. You've run hands-on training sessions with customers and adapted them in the room.
  • A track record of tying enablement to measurable outcomes such as ticket deflection, adoption, or time to value.
  • Experience influencing Product, Support, Delivery, and Marketing partners without direct authority.
  • The judgment to tell when a customer problem needs content, a training, or a product fix, and the writing skills to make the case.

Nice-to-haves:

  • Background in fintech, identity verification, fraud, or compliance.
  • Experience structuring knowledge bases for AI support agents or chatbots.
  • Hands-on experience with LMS, documentation, or in-product guidance tools.
  • Experience working inside a Product or Design organization.

Alloy is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. In addition to a competitive base salary, this position is also eligible for equity awards in the form of stock options (ISOs) as well as a competitive total benefits package. Your recruiter will be happy to walk you through the details and what compensation could look like for you specifically!

This position has a salary range of $180,000 to $220,000. 

Benefits and Perks

  • 401k with 100% match up to 4% of annual employee compensation

  • Hybrid work environment: Local employees are expected to work Tuesdays through Thursdays from our HQ in Union Square, Manhattan. Tasty lunches catered from a variety of local restaurants and frequent employee-organized cultural events contribute to our positive office energy. On Monday/Friday most employees Zoom into work from home while some take advantage of the quieter office.

How to apply

jobs.title: Sezzle: Chief Risk Officer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Nevada, Remote

Chief Risk Officer (CRO) – Sezzle Bank

Location: Nevada / Remote

Organization: Sezzle Bank (in formation)

Employment Type: Full-time | Remote

Reports To: President of Sezzle Bank and the Board Risk and Compliance Committee

About Sezzle:

With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We're not just transforming payments; we're redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we're building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you're excited about breaking new ground in tech and building products that make a real difference for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle.

About Sezzle Bank (in formation):

Sezzle Bank is a planned de novo national bank in formation, headquartered in Nevada and wholly owned by Sezzle Inc. The Bank will serve as the regulated banking entity supporting Sezzle's financial product offerings and ancillary services, with a strategic focus on responsible lending, financial innovation, and exceptional customer experience. We are building a best-in-class team to stand up a safe, sound, and compliant institution from the ground up.

About the Role:

We are seeking a highly experienced Chief Risk Officer to develop and maintain an effective, independent second-line risk management program for Sezzle Bank. The CRO will measure and manage credit, market, liquidity, and operational risk — with operational risk encompassing legal, compliance, and technology risk — as well as model-related risk across the Bank. Working with the Board and the Board Risk and Compliance Committee, the CRO will build the enterprise-wide risk governance framework that defines the Bank's risk culture, appetite, and limits, and will own the ongoing monitoring of these risks and of operational performance to ensure alignment with Board-approved policies and tolerances.

The CRO is a Bank-only executive with no concurrent Sezzle Inc. position and reports to the President of Sezzle Bank and to the Board Risk and Compliance Committee.

What You'll Do:

Risk Governance & Framework

  • Define enterprise-wide risk management strategies, policies, and the risk appetite framework; work with the Board and the Board Risk and Compliance Committee to establish the Bank's risk culture, appetite, and limits.
  • Identify, assess, measure, manage, monitor, and report on risk across the Bank, and ensure compliance with Board-approved policies, tolerances, and risk limits.
  • Identify emerging areas of risk, including potential risks associated with proposed new products and services, and ensure business strategies align with regulatory rules, guidance, and supervisory expectations.
  • Develop and maintain a model governance framework that includes independent model validation.
  • Participate in ALCO as the independent second-line risk perspective.

Regulatory & Examination Relationship

  • Serve as the Bank's primary relationship manager for the OCC Examiner-in-Charge, coordinating with the Bank's President.
  • Communicate with regulators and address regulatory inquiries and examination activities.
  • Serve as the Bank's designated CRA Officer: administer the CRA Strategic Plan, monitor the Bank's progress against its CRA performance commitments, and ensure CRA examination readiness.

Second-Line Oversight

  • Oversee the Bank's Chief Compliance Officer and the second-line compliance risk management function, including complaints handling and emerging regulatory and consumer compliance requirements.
  • Oversee the Bank's BSA Officer; ensure BSA/AML/OFAC policies, procedures, risk assessments, and controls are properly designed and operationally effective.
  • Oversee the Bank's Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) to ensure information assets, sensitive customer data, and technologies are protected; ensure the CISO reports routinely to the Board or the appropriate Board committee.

Board & Business Partnership

  • Serve as the primary source for all risk program communication and reporting to the Board and the Board Risk and Compliance Committee.
  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with business line management, effectively communicating emerging and present risk elements and issues.
  • Provide support and insight to the Bank's audit program, including addressing audit findings and remediation efforts.

What We Look For:

  • 15–20+ years of banking or financial services experience, with significant time in risk management, credit, compliance, or audit.
  • Minimum 7–10 years in a senior risk leadership role (CRO, SVP Risk, or equivalent) at a regulated financial institution.
  • Extensive experience managing a risk organization in a regulated banking environment, including direct experience with federal banking regulators (OCC, FDIC, or Federal Reserve) and the examination process.
  • Deep knowledge of enterprise risk management frameworks, banking regulatory requirements, and second-line governance.
  • Experience managing compliance, BSA/AML, OFAC, CRA, and cybersecurity risk programs.
  • Strong communication skills with Board-level risk reporting experience.
  • Demonstrated experience working with Claude or equivalent large language model tools is required; candidates must be comfortable leveraging AI to enhance productivity, research, and communication.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, or Mathematics; Master's degree preferred.
  • FRM (GARP), CERP (ABA), CAMS, CRCM, or CPA certification highly valued.
  • Experience with model risk governance and CECL/stress testing frameworks.
  • Prior experience with de novo bank formation or building a second-line risk function from the ground up.

About You:

  • You exhibit strong character. You do what you say you'll do and you do the right thing, even when no one is watching. You're a strong team member and secure enough to give others credit.

jobs.title: Dremio: Staff Software Engineer - Connectivity
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Portugal - Remote

Be Part of Building the Future

Dremio is the unified lakehouse platform for self-service analytics and AI, serving hundreds of global enterprises, including Maersk, Amazon, Regeneron, NetApp, and S&P Global. Customers rely on Dremio for cloud, hybrid, and on-prem lakehouses to power their data mesh, data warehouse migration, data virtualization, and unified data access use cases. Based on open source technologies, including Apache Iceberg and Apache Arrow, Dremio provides an open lakehouse architecture enabling the fastest time to insight and platform flexibility at a fraction of the cost.  Learn more at www.dremio.com.

About the role

Dremio's Connectivity team builds the high-performance connectivity solutions that help customers bring data to Dremio and connect Dremio to the broader data ecosystem. The team works across client drivers, protocols, connectors, interoperability, distributed systems, and the reliability and supportability of production data access.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll independently own multiple medium-to-large features or service components within a Connectivity and Clients area. You'll define the approach for a substantial team-area scope, turn ambiguous goals into clear milestones, make sound feature and service-level design decisions, and drive work through reliable production delivery. You will bring deep expertise in at least one area, such as JDBC or ODBC drivers, Apache Arrow ADBC, Arrow Flight SQL, BI interoperability, source connectivity, or connectivity reliability, while contributing effectively across adjacent areas. You will also mentor engineers and influence partner teams through strong technical judgment and execution.

What you'll be doing

  • Own substantial connectivity work: Lead multiple medium-to-large features or service components from problem definition through design, implementation, validation, release readiness, and operational handoff.
  • Turn ambiguity into an execution plan: Define reviewable milestones, acceptance measures, dependencies, estimates, and risks for complex customer, product, and engineering goals.
  • Design scalable, maintainable systems: Produce technical designs and architecture diagrams, explain trade-offs, and make feature and service-level decisions across drivers, protocols, client libraries, connectors, and distributed services.
  • Diagnose complex failures: Lead root-cause analysis across client/server, protocol, network, authentication, metadata, and distributed-system boundaries using logs, telemetry, profiles, benchmarks, and production evidence.
  • Build compatibility and reliability: Maintain API and protocol stability; create automated compatibility, interoperability, performance, scale, reliability, observability, and diagnostics coverage; and define practical migration paths for supported and legacy clients.
  • Collaborate and influence: Partner with Product, Query Execution, QA, Support, SRE, Documentation, and external technology partners to resolve dependencies and improve certification, customer experience, and supportability.
  • Raise the engineering bar: Participate actively in code and design reviews, mentor and coach engineers, improve team practices, and contribute to relevant upstream open-source projects when aligned with Dremio priorities.
  • Use AI-assisted development tools responsibly: Apply Dremio-approved AI tools to code comprehension, debugging, test generation, and documentation while protecting proprietary and customer data and validating results through review, testing, and sound engineering judgment.

What we're looking for

  • Staff-level ownership: 8+ years of production software engineering experience, or equivalent depth demonstrated through sustained ownership of complex systems and multiple substantial team-area features.
  • Programming expertise: Deep proficiency in Java, C++, Rust, Go, or another systems or services language, with the ability to work effectively in adjacent languages and frameworks.
  • Connectivity and systems depth: Experience designing and debugging APIs, protocols, client libraries, drivers, or distributed services, with strong knowledge of data structures, concurrency, asynchronous programming, networking, and failure handling.
  • Problem-solving ability: Able to identify and solve non-obvious problems across client/server and distributed-system boundaries and turn findings into durable fixes and regression coverage.
  • Quality mindset: Experience building comprehensive unit, integration, compatibility, performance, or reliability tests and working with production CI/CD, packaging, release, certification, and engineering quality controls.
  • Communication and influence: Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical trade-offs, surface risks early, align contributors across teams, and influence without formal authority.
  • Mentorship: Demonstrated ability to mentor and coach engineers and improve the effectiveness and engineering practices of the team around you.
  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degrees and equivalent industry experience are welcomed.

Bonus points if you have

  • Experience developing JDBC, ODBC, ADBC, or other database drivers.
  • Experience with Apache Arrow or Arrow Flight SQL.
  • Experience with SQL engines, databases, data platforms, or source connectors.
  • BI interoperability experience with Power BI, Tableau, Excel, or similar tools, including collaboration with partner engineering teams.
  • Knowledge of OAuth, OIDC, TLS, enterprise authentication, metadata discovery, or query pushdown.
  • Cross-platform native build, packaging, release engineering, compatibility certification, or upgrade support experience.
  • Observability, production diagnostics, customer escalation, long-running data transfer, cancellation, keepalive, timeout, or proxy experience.
  • Contributions to Apache Arrow or other relevant open-source projects.

What we value 

At Dremio, we hold ourselves to high standards when it comes to People, Thinking, and Action. Our Gnarlies (that's what we call our employees) communicate with clarity, drive accountability, and are respectful towards each other. We confront brutal facts and focus on results while operating with a sense of urgency and building a "flywheel". People who like to jump in and drive momentum will thrive in our #GnarlyLife.

Dremio is an equal opportunity employer supporting workforce diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other unlawful factor.

Dremio is committed to providing any necessary accommodations for individuals with disabilities within our application and interview process. To request accommodation due to a disability, please inform your recruiter.

Dremio has policies in place to protect the personal information that employees and applicants disclose to us. Please click here to review the privacy notice. 

Important Security Notice for Candidates

At Dremio, we uphold trust and transparency as paramount values in all our interactions with customers, partners, employees, and the general public. We have been targeted by individuals creating fake domains similar to ours to scam prospects and candidates. Please note that all official communications from us will be from an @dremio.com domain. If you suspect you've been targeted by a scam, it's imperative to report the incident to your local law enforcement agencies. For more information about this type of scam, please refer to Dremio's official statement here.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote

The Voice AI space is at an inflection point; we’re looking for folks truly excited to join a small team and help define the future of the industry.

We are one of the most capital-efficient AI companies on the planet - with under 100 people generating roughly $600K ARR per employee, we sit among the top 5 most revenue-dense teams within the fastest-growing AI companies today. That's not an accident; it's a deliberate choice to stay lean, move fast, and give every person on the team outsized ownership and impact. With thousands of customers including Granola, Fireflies, Figure AI, and CallRail, the company has real scale - processing over 2 million hours of audio daily and handling more than 1 million API calls every day. This is a rare growth-stage opportunity where the business is proven and the trajectory is steep, but the team is still small enough that your fingerprints are on everything.

If you've ever felt buried under layers of bureaucracy, starved of real ownership, or frustrated watching your work disappear into a slow-moving org, AssemblyAI is built differently. The company operates as a true meritocracy, with no heavy planning or approval processes and no gatekeeping on the tools or information you need. For anyone who genuinely cares about voice AI, not as a trend to chase, but as a technology to build,  this is the place where the most interesting problems at the most interesting scale are being solved by a team small enough that you'll actually know everyone's name.

We’re committed to creating a space where our employees can bring their full selves to work and have equal opportunity to succeed. No matter your race, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, origin, ability, age, veteran status, if joining this mission speaks to you, we encourage you to apply!

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Research Engineer to join our Research team, developing and improving the systems behind large-scale distributed training, data processing, and inference. Our goal as an organization is to solve customer problems and improve our products quickly through model development and measurement — and how fast we move depends on how quickly anyone here can run an experiment, measure it, and find out what's wrong. Raising that ceiling is the heart of this role. You'll be working inside the pipeline you're improving, not alongside it.

The ideal candidate has a deep understanding of modern deep learning systems, combined with strong engineering expertise across JAX and TPUs, layer-level optimization, large-scale distributed training, streaming, low-latency and asynchronous inference, inference compilers, and advanced parallelization techniques.

This is a cross-functional role. You'll work closely with our researchers, our infrastructure team, and production engineering — not as a handoff point, but as the person who learns enough of each domain to follow problems through to resolution. At times you'll train models, run evaluations, and analyze data yourself, both to deliver impact directly and to learn what's worth building to multiply the team's work. The bar is someone who understands the end-to-end impact they intend to make, measures it from the outset, and would rather find out they were wrong in a week than in a quarter. That discipline is what turns cross-functional ownership into an advantage.

The role is embedded within the Research team. 

What You’ll Do

  • Raise the team's experimental velocity — make it faster to launch an experiment job, get a number back you can trust, and know what to try next.
  • Maintain and evolve our JAX training framework, keeping it scalable and efficient for large-scale distributed training runs on TPU.
  • Improve the data our models learn from: investigating quality issues, building the tooling to surface them, and turning what you find into measurable accuracy gains.
  • Analyze the accuracy of production models, build evaluation harnesses, and work out which improvements will matter most to customers.
  • Translate research prototypes into production-ready systems, refactoring and modernizing model architectures and infrastructure along the way.
  • Optimize production inference for speech language models, both from a serving architecture perspective and through advanced techniques such as quantization and speculative decoding.
  • Investigate and resolve performance bottlenecks across the stack, from low-level kernels (XLA, Pallas) to high-level system design.
  • Partner with researchers, infrastructure, and production engineering to trace problems to their real source and ship fixes that hold.

What You’ll Need

  • Expert-level proficiency with JAX and TPUs, including the surrounding ecosystem (Flax, Optax, the XLA compilation pipeline).
  • Measurement discipline. You define what success looks like before you start, you stay skeptical of your own results until they hold up, and you treat an unexplained improvement as a problem rather than a win.
  • Appetite for the whole pipeline. Your core strength might be JAX and TPU performance, but when a customer issue traces back to a data problem or an evaluation blind spot, you want to go find it yourself. The people who do well here went deep in one area first, then kept expanding outward.
  • Strong experience optimizing inference systems for production, ideally with LLMs or speech models.
  • Deep understanding of distributed training at scale, modern deep learning systems, and ML infrastructure best practices.
  • Familiarity with modern inference optimization techniques: continuous batching, KV-cache management, sharding strategies, quantization.
  • Enthusiasm for refactoring and improving existing systems — you thrive on making products and code faster and better.
  • Strong Python skills; C++ or Rust experience for kernel-level work is a plus.
  • Excellent communication and a collaborative mindset — you can clearly explain complex tradeoffs and prioritize high-impact work.

Bonus

  • Domain knowledge in Speech-to-Text: ASR architectures, audio processing, streaming inference.
